notes.title: Dimensional - full release now live
notes.notes:
I'm pleased to announce that the full release of Dimensional is now live.

If you played the early access version, I highly recommend starting the game from the beginning. There have been lots of changes over the months.

Thanks to all the people that provided feedback, reported bugs and helped test the game. Watching videos of people playing the game was especially useful too, so thank you for those :)

I hope you enjoy it. If you do, please tell your friends and help me spread the word about my indie game.

notes.title: Progress update
notes.notes:
I'm now working on the final level of Dimensional and we are drawing closer to the full release.

[h1]The plan[/h1]

[list]
[*] Nov - Release patch with support for Oculus Touch
[*] Dec - Final beta testing
[*] Dec - Release version 1.0.0
[/list]

Version 1.0.0 will bring 3 new levels, more narrative and general improvements.

If you know of any bugs or parts of the game that were too hard or frustrating, please let me know so I can fix them for the final release.

Thanks for supporting the project during the early access stage. If you've enjoyed playing the game so far, please encourage your friends to add it to their wishlist in preparation for the final release. Thank you.

notes.title: Patch 0.3.7 fixes problems starting the game
notes.notes:
The patch released today should fix two problems for Oculus Rift users. 

* The game now doesn't crash when loaded without the "-vr" command line option
* You should not see a message about not owning the game.

If anyone else still has problems please try uninstalling then reinstalling the game to ensure the change from 32bit to 64bit copied all required files.

Please let me know if you have any issues in the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/457340]Community Hub[/url]

notes.title: Halloween update + 64bit
notes.notes:
[h1]Halloween update[/h1]

A new update has been released today including a Halloween challenge in the Trials level. This points-based trial is intended as a bit of fun for you and your friends. Use Digby to smash deadly pumpkins before they get to you. Smash them using parts of the environment for extra points. Push them into fans, electric walls or spikes. Activate the gigantic pendulum to take out loads of them, shout at the voice sensor to fire bullets or squash them by dropping high platforms on them.

This update is included in the free demo for the next 10 days, but will remain in the full game permanently.
[url=https://youtu.be/WSCpQSHBFZ4]Watch video[/url]

See how high you can climb on the [url=http://steamcommunity.com//stats/457340/leaderboards/1485486]online leaderboard[/url] (doesn't include demo version)

 
[h1]64 bit version[/h1]

Due to some limitations in the version of the game engine I'm using, this release is 64bit only. This is already a minimum requirements for the Oculus headset, but If any of you are not running a 64bit O/S please let me know and I will investigate doing a separate 32bit non-Oculus version.

[h1]Other changes[/h1]

You will also notice more changes as part of the ongoing UI improvements. The targeting displays for the teleporting and Digby have been improved in this release. I've also removed the blue directional arrows that guided your attention forwards. Instead the teleport icon helps you keep your sense of orientation in your physical room.

Hope you have a great Halloween :)

notes.title: Patch 0.2.2.0 - new level 6 + new trial + important bug fixes
notes.notes:
[h1]New content[/h1]

[b]Level 6[/b] experiments with tight spaces and attempts to make you feel a little claustrophobic in places. It includes two optional secret messages and obscure areas to find and access. Digby also gets another temporary power-up to play with.

[b]The new trial “Blocks”[/b], has you smashing blocks before they smash you to see if you can get a [url=http://steamcommunity.com/stats/457340/leaderboards/1430683]high score[/url].

[h1]Bug fixes and changes[/h1]
Taller players have experienced a problem where they couldn’t teleport to a beacon. This should now be resolved.

Previously you weren’t allowed to teleport to Digby’s location if it would result in your head colliding with him. It’s likely that you didn’t notice Digby was in the way and thought the teleporting was just faulty. Now Digby will just move out of the way.

You can no longer be killed during a teleport while you’re in limbo.

Previous levels will keep getting improvements as well as fixes. As an example, you will find a voice activated food dispenser on level 3. Some more rewards for my Kickstarter backers are also being introduced, so you will see their names included in various levels.

Please let me know in the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/457340]community forums[/url] if you get stuck or find bugs.

More content is on the way next month.

Thanks for playing.

notes.title: Patch 0.2.0.10
notes.notes:
I’ve been on holiday recently (which was greatly needed), so expect more changes and improvements going forward.

[b]Recalling Digby[/b]
You can now make Digby immediately teleport to your position by pressing Y on your gamepad, or left grip button on your Vive controller.

[b]Limbo[/b]
Graphics of limbo have been toned down to be less "trippy" as requested by a few players.

[b]New Vive FPS controller option[/b]
By default in FPS mode you physically face forward in your room and then use your trackpads to rotate and drive your playing area around as in a traditional FPS-style game. This encourages you to keep returning to your forward position to optimise tracking and help you keep an awareness of your orientation in your real room.

A new option in the Gameplay menu, allows you to change this behaviour so that the forward direction is considered to be the direction of your laser pointer. The advantage of this approach is that you don’t have to use artificial rotation. Instead you physically turn the direction you want to travel, point your laser forwards and just press forward (or backward or strafe). You can still use the trackpad for artificial rotation too.

[b]Optional forward indicators[/b]
By default, blue transparent indicators remind you which direction is forward. This is one of the ways I try to keep you facing forward for optimum tracking. It also helps you be aware of your orientation in your real room, which should help you stay relaxed and immersed rather than relying on the chaperone unexpectedly popping up and breaking your immersion.

On the Vive with a large playing area, the indicators may be annoying to some, so a new option in the Gameplay menu allows you to hide the indicators.

[b]Teleport bug[/b]
A bug has been fixed where you sometimes couldn't teleport to a small specific area in front of you, where the drone appears that gives you occasional advice.

[b]Extending the Oculus tracking boundary[/b]
Quietly released in a previous update, there is now a menu option for Oculus Rift users that allows you to extend the length of the tracking volume. This allows people with large rooms to move beyond the recommended tracking area without seeing the red mesh appear. Tracking may be less reliable further away from the camera, but I leave you to experiment and see what works for you.

 + more fixes and improvements

notes.title: News update
notes.notes:
Just a quick update to let you know what's happening.

[b]July[/b]
July releases will focus on improving the existing levels and mechanisms. This includes:
* Extra checks to ensure everyone's Vive controllers are behaving
* Investigating improved FPS controls
* Testing bluetooth headphones
* Tracking bug where positional audio can die until game is restarted
* Changing limbo graphics to be less "trippy"
* Remove gaze-focused blue dot for HTC Vive and instead use laser pointer rather than gaze to activate HUD info on droids.
* Look at fast-return option for Digby so you don't have to wait up to 5 seconds when he gets stuck.
* General improvements to existing levels

Let me know if I'm missing anything that's stopping you playing the game.

[b]August[/b]
August will bring new levels.

notes.title: Patch 0.2.0.7
notes.notes:
Some important fixes in this patch include:

[b]Positional teleporting - missing GO icon[/b]
Sometimes when you were asked to move over the GO icon during a positional teleport, the icon would be missing. I couldn't reproduce this but believe it was due to an incorrect startup sequence. It shouldn't happen now, but if it does: 1) please tell me. 2) the reset button on your controller will allow you to return to the last check point.

[b]Teleporting into walls[/b]
If quickly teleporting around a room it was possible to end up in limbo due to being in a wall when you completed the teleport. You cannot teleport within 5cm or so of a wall now, which should fix the issue.

[b]FPS-mode stuttering[/b]
When in FPS mode it would stutter as you moved along a sloped wall. It should now move smoothly.

Other minor fixes are included too.

Thanks for reporting the issues.

Also, I wrote [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/457340/discussions/0/365172408529471637/]some notes[/url] about the difficulty of the game and my plans. Feel free to comment.

notes.title: Changes to jumping
notes.notes:
Thanks for the useful feedback on jumping. 

Some changes are now live that I hope will make it more enjoyable for you.

[b]1) If you are off the floor when the laser passes, you should clear it.[/b] Previously I used a collision detection where your feet where calculated (poorly) to be. Cheating will still fail, such as standing on a chair, because it constantly checks your height. You will probably be able to jump over them while jumping forwards now too. I've left the advice to jump straight up because that's the safest way to complete the task.

2) If you just don't want to be noisily jumping around or have a low ceiling, or a bad leg, you can now disable jumping in the new "Gameplay" menu option.

There's not going to be lots of jumping in the game, but I felt it was an interesting mechanism to try and hopefully with the two options everyone should be able to finish and enjoy it.

I would be interested to hear from some of the players who struggled to see if it feels OK now.

I'd like to keep experimenting with new ideas, situations and gameplay mechanisms during Early Access. I hope that's what you want as well. Your feedback is important to help me get it right, or throw it out.

notes.notes:
One of my players is still having problems with his Vive controller when shooting Digby. I'm trying this patch to make the right trigger fire slightly earlier to see if it helps.

I'll be reworking the Vive trigger coding next week, but please let me know if this makes things any worse or better for any of you in the meantime.

notes.title: Quick patch 0.2.0.4
notes.notes:
Some players have experienced issues with their Vive controllers not firing Digby unless they manually make sure the trigger is fully released. I've reduced the sensitivity a little on the trigger to try and prevent this, together with some other changes. My controllers work fine, so can the people who experienced this please let me know if it resolves the issue or if further tuning is required.

In the laser jumping in level 3 I've added a sign to tell you to jump straight up to get over the lasers. Jumping forwards wasn't intended due to safety concerns and also makes it much harder to clear due to the way the jump mechanism works. Short term there is also a little debug box that shows where your feet are so you can see how the system is calculating your jump height. You will also see indicators in front of you showing your height and current position. I'd like to hear if it doesn't seem to work right for you.

Thanks to everyone who has provided feedback or bug reports. I will be spending next week implementing fixes and improvements.

I hope you're all enjoying the game.
If you are, remember to tell your friends
If you're not, please tell me what I need to fix :)
